LESSON: MUSLIM SCHOLARS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Islamic Heritage
Topic 7.2: Muslim scholars
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 7

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Muslim scholars, part of Islamic Heritage in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How did the contributions of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu impact on Muslims?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or on available reference materials the contributions of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy (1912-1982) and Aisha Lemu (1940-2019) and make class presentations,

2. research on the biographies of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu (early life, educational background, contributions and achievements), make summary notes and present in class,

3. brainstorm on the lessons learnt from the biographies of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu and present in class,

4. discuss on the possible ways of emulating Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in groups, make notes and present in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or on available reference materials the contributions of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy (1912-1982) and Aisha Lemu (1940-2019) and make class presentations,
2. research on the biographies of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu (early life, educational background, contributions and achievements), make summary notes and present in class,
3. brainstorm on the lessons learnt from the biographies of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu and present in class,
4. discuss on the possible ways of emulating Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in groups, make notes and present in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Muslim scholars together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital Literacy: the skills of interacting with digital technology and connecting with technology enhanced as learners search

online the contributions of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy (1912-1982) and Aisha Lemu (1940-2019) and make class

presentations

● Communication and Collaboration: the skills of listening, speaking, writing and teamwork enhanced as learners brainstorm

on the lessons learnt from the biographies of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in groups and present in class

● Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively enhanced as learners buzz on the possible ways of emulating Sheikh

Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in groups and make charts

● Self-efficacy: effective communication skills enhanced as learners brainstorm on the lessons learnt from the biographies of

Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in groups and present in class

Values:
● Responsibility enhanced as learners buzz on possible ways of emulating Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu

and make charts

● Unity enhanced as learners buzz on the possible ways of emulating Sheikh Abdallah Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in

groups and make charts

● Respect enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinion as they buzz on the possible ways of emulating Sheikh Abdallah

Saleh Al-Farsy and Aisha Lemu in groups and make charts

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: assertiveness enhanced as learners brainstorm on the lessons learnt from the biographies of Sheikh Abdallah Saleh
